title: Council endorses Councillor Wilton for FCM committees
subtitle: A brief late-agenda meeting also covered the confirming by-law and adjournment, with no other business.
overview: Centre Wellington Council held a short meeting on August 13, 2025, with one substantive item. Council endorsed Councillor Bronwynne Wilton to serve on committees of the Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM) Board of Directors {{vote:m1}}.

The endorsement runs from June 2025 to the end of the current term of Council in November 2026. Council also agreed to cover the costs of Councillor Wilton attending FCM meetings. FCM advocates to the federal government on behalf of municipalities, so the role gives the township a closer link to that work.

Councillor Wilton said the interest grew from work with FCM on a rural Canada report, and committee placement depends on FCM's selection process. Wilton committed to sharing what is learned with Council and staff. Council then passed the confirming by-law and adjourned. No other business was dealt with.

decisions.detail: Council endorsed Councillor Bronwynne Wilton to serve on FCM Board of Directors committees from June 2025 to November 2026 and agreed to cover the associated meeting costs {{vote:m1}}.

debate: Councillor Wilton explained that recent work with FCM on a rural Canada report built familiarity with its staff and advocacy, and said the township could be better connected to federal-level issues.

Wilton clarified the request is for FCM committees, not the board, and that FCM would place applicants on a committee based on their skills and interests. Wilton did not know how competitive the process is.
Councillors spoke in support, saying more representation at other levels of government is increasingly important and that they welcome colleagues putting their names forward.
Wilton said that if selected, information from the role would be shared with Council and staff in a timely way.
